desc:
A street is modelled as a number line. Each lamp is a pair [position, radius] and lights every integer point from position - radius to position + radius inclusive.

The brightness of an integer point is the number of lamps that light it. Return the smallest integer point whose brightness is the maximum over the whole street.

lamps = [[1, 2], [3, 1]]
result = 2

The first lamp lights -1..3, the second lights 2..4. Points 2 and 3 both have brightness 2, and the smaller one is 2.
hints: The street is far too long to look at point by point, but only a few points can matter. Which points can be where the brightness first reaches its maximum?
Brightness only goes up at the left end of a lamp's interval and only goes down just after its right end.

Create events (position - radius, +1) and (position + radius + 1, -1), sort them, sweep with a running total, and remember the first coordinate where the total exceeds the best so far. Apply all events of one coordinate before comparing.
editorial: This is a difference array on a huge coordinate range, so we keep it sparse: each lamp contributes +1 at its left end and -1 one past its right end. Sorting the event coordinates and sweeping gives the brightness on each stretch between consecutive events.

The maximum is first reached at some left end, so it is enough to compare the running total after all events of a coordinate have been applied (departures at coordinate x belong to lamps that no longer light x). Updating the answer only on a strict improvement returns the smallest position. Time O(m log m), space O(m).
